2. The petitioner is facing trial in the court of learned Adhoc Additional District and Sessions Judge (FTSC), Keonjhar having been charged under Sections 363/366/376(3)/376(2)(n)/323/ 294/506 of the I.P.C., 1860 and Section 6 of the POCSO Act in Special Case No.20 of 2024 arising out of Pandapada P.S. Case No.101 of 2024.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge (FTSC), Keonjhar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. During trial, till yet, eight numbers of witnesses have already been examined including the victim/informant as P.W.2.

The victim(P.W.2) has deposed in her evidence during trial stating that, the petitioner had taken her(victim) to his house and they had lived together in the house of the accused/petitioner, wherein the petitioner had kept sexual relationship with her(victim), as a result of which, the victim became pregnant and delivered a female child at the hospital.

After giving delivery to a female child,
she(victim) intimated the same to her mother and her mother sent Rs.200/- to her(victim) through pay Phonepe, to which, the victim received and then, she(victim) came from the house of the petitioner to her parents' house, for which, the petitioner came to the parents' house of the victim and quarreled with her.
Therefore, she(victim) lodged the F.I.R against the petitioner.
Basing upon such F.I.R., a case was registered and investigation was started.
4. During investigation, the petitioner was arrested on 22.02.2024 and forwarded to the court and since then, the petitioner is in custody.

The victim(P.W.2) has also deposed in her cross- examination during trial that, during her staying in the house of the petitioner, she had not contacted her parents over phone, but, the brother-in-law of the petitioner had intimated the parents of the victim(P.W.2) regarding her staying in the house Rama Munda vs State Of Odisha on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37950911/
1 of the petitioner, but, her parents did not come to the house of the petitioner in spite of knowing about her(victim's) staying in the house of the petitioner.

entities.text: Rama Munda vs State Of Odisha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per F.I.R., the petitioner had stayed for three days in the parents' house of the victim.

As per the deposition of the victim(P.W.2), if the petitioner would have taken her(victim) with him(petitioner), then, she would not have reported the matter at the P.S. She(victim) has also deposed in her deposition that, it is a fact that, the petitioner had not threatened her(victim) to kill and her baby girl and she(victim) is interested to stay with the petitioner as his wife and not to proceed further in this case.
5. Taking the above evidence of the victim(P.W.2) during trial, I find no justification to disallow the prayer for bail of the petitioner.
6. Therefore, the bail application filed by the petitioner is allowed.

7. He(petitioner) is allowed to go on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/-(rupees fifty thousand) with two solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned court in seisin over the matter with conditions that:-
(i) he(petitioner) shall not involve with similar nature of crime in future.

(ii) he shall not terrorize, coerce, influence or threat any witnesses of the prosecution including the informant and her family members either directly or indirectly in any manner whatsoever at any stage of the proceeding of the case.

(iii) he shall appear before the trial court personally in each dater of adjournment of the case without fail, but, in case of his failure to comply any of the aforesaid conditions, the court in seisin over the matter is authorized to cancel his bail order outrightly without seeking any permission for the same from this Court.
8.
Accordingly, the bail application filed by the petitioner is disposed of finally.

9. Grant certified copy of this order to the petitioner on proper application.
( A.C. Behera )
